newsitem.title: UK: RUGBY UNION-GOMARSALL MAKES SPARKLING DEBUT.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-GOMARSALL MAKES SPARKLING DEBUT.

text.p: New cap Andy Gomarsall collected two of England's seven tries on Saturday as Phil de Glanville marked his first game as national captain with a comfortable 54-21 win over Italy.

The Wasps' scrum-half, one of five new caps in the lineup, touched down once in each half and was at the heart of an England effort which showed flashes of invention but was not as convincing as the final scoreline suggested.
The English attempted to play the expansive game that they had promised but in the end it was the strength of their forwards which made the difference.
"I have never played with a pack of forwards that were so dominant," de Glanville said. "And all the new guys were superb. I told them they had to contribute all through and they did."

Italy played well below their capacity in the first half and were trailing 28-0 at the break after fly-half Mike Catt's two early penalties had been followed by tries by Gomarsall, wing Jon Sleightholme and flanker Lawrence Dallaglio.
Sleightholme's try was cleverly worked by Catt who chipped over the Italian defence, allowing the Bath wing to gather and twist through a tackle before dotting down.
Catt, despite missing two simple kicks at goal, had a productive afternoon with the boot, as he kicked three penalties and converted five of the tries for a tally of 19 points.

The Italians leaked another try when lock Martin Johnson bullied his way over three minutes into the second half but they found their feet and scored three tries from wing Paulo Vaccari, scrum-half Alessando Troncon and number eight Orazio Arancio.

The first from Vacarri was the best of the match. Coming off the right wing he collected an inside pass from fly-half Diego Dominguez and broke through the first line of defence before jinking past full-back Tim Stimpson.

England, however, had the stronger and fitter pack and forced their way back to the Italian line. A scrum five metres out ended with Gomersall evading flanker Corrado Covi's weak tackle and getting through for the score.
He was then followed in the last few minutes by solo efforts from flanker Tim Rodber and number eight Chris Sheasby, another new cap.

England's final total of international debutants rose to seven when hooker Phil Greening and prop Rob Hardwick came on as late replacements for Mark Regan and Jason Leonard, who was winning his 50th cap.
"I was surprised and pleased with what we had achieved," said England coach Jack Rowell. "It was better than I had expected."

England - 15-Tim Stimpson; 14-Jon Sleightholme, 13-Will Carling, 12-Jeremy Guscott, 11-Adedayo Adebayo; 10-Mike Catt, 9-Andy Gomersall (Kyran Bracken); 8-Chris Sheasby, 7-Tim Rodber, 6-Lawrence Dallaglio, 5-Martin Johnson, 4-Simon Shaw, 3-Graham Rowntree, 2-Mark Regan (Phil Greening), 1-Jason Leonard (Rob Hardwick) .

Italy - 15-Javier Pertile; 14-Paolo Vaccari, 13-Ivan Francescato, 12-Stefano Bordon, 11-Leandro Manteri, 10-Diego Dominguez, 9-Alessandro Troncon; 8-Orazio Arancio, 7-Corrado Covi (Andrea Sgorlon), 6-Massimo Giovanelli (captain); 5-Carlo Checchinato (Andrea Barattin), 4-Walter Cristofoletto, 3-Franco Properzi Curti, 2-Carlo Orlandi, 1-Massimo Cuttita.
